title: Coron vs El Nido: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Coron for diving, snorkeling, and unique geological wonders. El Nido for beaches, lagoon variety, and nightlife. Do both via the Ultimate Expedition if you have 10+ days.

categories.name: Beaches & Lagoons
categories.summary: El Nido has more beach and lagoon variety — 45+ islands, four tour routes, and Nacpan Beach. Coron's Malcapuya is exceptional but fewer options overall.

categories.name: Diving & Snorkeling
categories.summary: Coron's WWII wrecks and unique lakes (Kayangan, Barracuda) are world-class. Marine life is more abundant and coral healthier than El Nido.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Both are affordable, but Coron has slightly cheaper accommodation and much cheaper flights (Cebu Pacific to Busuanga vs Airswift monopoly to El Nido).

categories.name: Nightlife & Food
categories.summary: El Nido's Calle Hama strip has genuine restaurant and bar variety. Coron is a quiet working town with limited evening options.

categories.name: Crowds
categories.summary: El Nido's peak-season group tours can have 20+ boats at the same spots. Coron is generally less crowded.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: El Nido has the van option from Puerto Princesa (cheap, just long). Coron requires a separate flight to Busuanga. El Nido is more accessible.

faq.question: Is Coron or El Nido better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: El Nido is easier for first-timers; Coron is better if diving is a priority.

faq.question: How do you get from Coron to El Nido?
faq.answer: The Ultimate Expedition — a 3-day, 2-night ferry — is the recommended route (₱2,500–3,500). Flying via Manila is the alternative.

faq.question: What's the best time to visit?
faq.answer: November to May (dry season). February–April is the sweet spot.
